newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: CRICKET-DE SILVA ENDS BARREN RUN WITH 168.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-DE SILVA ENDS BARREN RUN WITH 168.

text.p: Sri Lankan vice-captain Aravinda de Silva ended a barren run of 14 test innings without a century on Wednesday by compiling 168 as the first test against Pakistan ended in a draw.
Sri Lanka, resuming at 206 for three, batted out the whole of the final day to finish on 423 for eight.

The highlight of the day was de Silva's marathon knock. In 508 minutes at the wicket he hardly put a foot wrong and his only false stroke resulted in his dismisal when he was caught by Saqlain Mushtaq at mid-off off Mushtaq Ahmed.
De Silva had faced 383 balls and hit one six and 14 fours in compiling his ninth test century, his fifth against Pakistan and his highest at home.
His last century for his country in September 1995 came against Pakistan at Faisalabad while his previous highest score at home was 148 against India in 1993-94.
Left-handers Hashan Tillekeratne and Sanath Jayasuriya, the latter having recovered from a virus which prevented him from taking the field on Tuesday, chipped in with contrasting half-centuries.
Tillekeratne followed his first innings century with 54 made in 105 minutes with five fours.
Jayasuriya showed no signs of his illness as he smashed one six and seven fours on his way to an exciting 62 off 84 balls which enlivened the afternoon session.
The match ended after one ball of the final 15 mandatory overs had been bowled.

Off-spinner Saqlain Mushtaq put up another marathon bowling effort to pick up four for 137 from 63 overs. His match bag of nine wickets coupled with 58 in Pakistan's only innings earned him the "Man of the Match" award.
